It’s been over a year now, this feeling. Just… heavy. Like I'm wading through thick mud every single day. Getting myself to the toll booth feels like climbing a mountain. I used to enjoy the little chats with the regulars, but now I just want to be left alone. My mind feels cloudy, like there's a fog in my head, and it’s hard to concentrate on anything. Honestly, sometimes I think about just driving my car into the barrier, or just letting go of the wheel on my way home. It feels like a plan, sometimes.

And then there are the voices. They whisper things, sometimes nice, sometimes not. They tell me I’m special, that I have a gift, and that I'm destined for something great, more than just this booth. Nobody else seems to hear them, though. It’s strange, because sometimes I hear them even when I don't feel quite so down, but it's mostly when the dark cloud is really heavy. It just adds to the confusion.
D015-D007_h001.question_a:
"It's been over a year now, more like thirteen, fourteen months, since this dark cloud settled over me. I just feel so… heavy. Getting out of bed for work at the toll booth feels like lifting a truck, and once I’m there, I just go through the motions. All the joy from the little things in life, gone. My mind feels like it's constantly slogging through mud; I can't think straight or focus on anything. Most days, I just want it all to end. I’ve pictured it, you know, just driving right off the bridge on my way home, or maybe just not waking up.

And then there are these… moments. I hear voices sometimes, whispering my name, or telling me I'm special, destined for something great, chosen for some important task. It’s hard to explain, but it feels so real, like those voices are imparting some profound truth about my hidden power. But these things only happen when I’m really deep in this slump, you know, when I feel the lowest. Once I feel even a tiny bit better, the voices and these thoughts about being special, they just, poof, disappear."
D015-D007_h001.question_b:
It's been over a year now, and I just feel… heavy. Most days, it's a monumental effort to even get out of bed, let alone face another shift in that booth. My mind feels foggy, like I'm trying to think through a thick haze. I just don't have the drive for anything anymore. Honestly, there are times I think about how easy it would be to just… not wake up. I’ve gone over it in my head—the best way, the best time.

But lately, there's been something else. I hear things, whispers really, telling me I'm destined for something great, that I have a special gift no one understands. Like I'm meant to transcend this dull existence. And I know it's real, even though the voices sometimes stop for stretches. Sometimes, for a couple of weeks at a time, I don't feel quite so low, but the whispers and that feeling of being chosen, they don't go away. They just… persist. Even when the heavy sadness lifts a bit, those thoughts and voices are still there, clear as day. Then the gloom always comes back, taking over again, and that's usually where I am.

Like my bad luck, or bad driving, is somehow spreading. I keep trying to shake it off, but I just can’t. Sometimes, especially when I’m driving, I have these sudden, awful urges to just swerve into oncoming traffic, or step off a bridge when I’m on a break. I don’t want to act on them, but the thoughts are so powerful.

And it’s not just that. I keep getting this strange, metallic smell, like something’s burning, even when there's nothing there. And lately, it feels like people are watching me, especially on my route. I’m starting to think some of the other drivers, maybe even the dispatchers, are in on it, like they’re trying to catch me doing something wrong. It’s all so much, and it really only started when this whole depressed feeling took over. It’s making it impossible to focus on my job; I’m scared I’m going to cause a real accident.

Sometimes, driving the bus, I get this overwhelming urge to just… swerve into oncoming traffic, or step in front of a train when I'm waiting at the station. Lately, things have gotten even weirder. There are these strange smells, like burning rubber or something metallic, that no one else seems to notice. I even heard them whispering about me on the bus a few times, though I can't quite make out what they're saying. This surveillance has been going on for a while now, even during those brief times when I feel a little bit more like myself and the sadness lifts a bit.
